items.title: Restrictive permissions / no bypass permissions on Claude Projects
items.body:
**What happened**
What happened:
In Claude Projects / Remote Control sessions (folder-connected cloud threads), the session is forced into Auto mode with no option to switch to Bypass permissions (--dangerously-skip-permissions).

The Auto mode classifier is also overly conservative and blocks SSH, production deploy scripts, and other commands that previously worked — even when explicit allow rules exist in project settings / settings.json. Compound commands, slight variations, or commands that follow other actions frequently fall through to the classifier and get blocked. It evaluates calls in isolation and doesn’t seem to respect prior approvals given in the same thread.

What I expected:

Ability to set Bypass permissions for a Project / Remote Control thread (at least when starting from the terminal), the same way it’s possible in regular Claude Code sessions.
Allow rules in settings to actually exempt the listed commands (including reasonable variations) from the classifier.
Or, at minimum, the classifier to ask instead of hard-blocking when it is uncertain, and to honor prior chat approvals.
This is currently making production and remote workflows significantly more painful than regular Claude Code sessions. Happy to provide specific command examples or thread IDs if useful.

**Environment**
- Filed from: Report a problem in Claude Code

items.title: studio monitor blind to Claude Code permission prompt
items.body:
## Objective

During #1259 a member subagent ran `rm -rf /fake`. Claude Code drew "Dangerous rm operation on critical path" Yes/No prompt. Bypass-permissions mode on; prompt still blocks. Sat ~3h. `fleet ls` ACTIVITY showed "? claude not on screen". No alert, no heal, no nudge. Blocked studio looked like unknown-idle.

Likely same classifier family as #1267: modal rows not recognized as claude frame (`readActivityFrame`, apps/fleet/src/studio/activity.ts; `footerAtBottom`, apps/fleet/src/studio/failover.ts).

Need:
- Classifier detects permission/confirm modal (rows like "Do you want to proceed?", numbered option rows `❯ 1. Yes`, "Esc to cancel") → distinct activity kind (e.g. `blocked_on_prompt`), never "claude not on screen".
- Alert surfaces to maestro after N min blocked (board/monitor-visible line).
- Never auto-answer. Destructive prompt waits for human.

Refs #1267 #1259.

## Output format

PR: activity kind for permission modal + alert path. Fixture: captured pane with "Dangerous rm operation" modal under bypass-mode footer (main + member panel variants). Tests: modal frame → blocked kind; alert emits after threshold; idle/working/DEAD_FRAME classification unchanged. Failing test first.

## Boundaries

Touch apps/fleet/src/studio activity/failover classifier, alert emit, tests. No keystrokes into modal, no auto-approve. No container/ change; if hook needed, flag in PR (image window). Merge only on green gate/verdict.

---

items.body:
A cell type (or a `claude-code` provider for `ore:ai`) that calls `claude -p` with the user's Claude Code login instead of an API key: no second account, and the Claude Code account's policies (rules, permission modes, hooks, managed settings) apply.

Points to settle:
- It needs the desktop session's login, so it runs on the host, not in a container: an explicit opt-in per workflow on top of `permissions`.
- A host-side `claude` with a `Read` tool bypasses the container mount that enforces `vaultRead`: run it with no read tools, or a working directory limited to what `vaultRead` allows.
- Read-only `--tools` by default, `--permission-prompts none`, writes only through VaultOre's own output.
- `--output-format json`, with cost and turns in the run artifact; `--max-budget-usd` as a per-cell cap; `--no-session-persistence`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1`; strip the parent session's `CLAUDE*` variables.
- `--bare` is unusable: it never reads OAuth or the keychain. `--max-turns` was not in `claude --help` (2.1.296); find the supported turn limit.
- E2E test with a stub `claude` on `PATH`.

items.title: Permission modes like Claude Code: Ask, Accept edits, Plan and Bypass

labels.name: feature
labels.description: A feature you can test end to end

items.body:
**What you get.** You choose how much a job asks you, like Claude Code's modes, per job or as the default:

- **Ask:** every command and file edit waits for you as a card: *Yes* · *Yes, and don't ask again for `swift test` in oby* · *No, and tell it what to do instead* (typed or spoken).
- **Accept edits:** edits inside the job's worktree go through, and commands ask.
- **Plan:** the agent only reads, then brings a plan as a decision card. Approving it runs the job in the mode you pick.
- **Bypass:** Oby answers everything itself, as it does today.

The fixed rules hold in every mode, Bypass included: no push or posting (only Publish does), the worktree only, no background work, only Tetrix's reads among MCP tools, and no secrets. Bypass skips questions, not fences.

## Test it when it's done

- [ ] Settings › Permissions defaults to Bypass (today's behaviour). A job dispatched in Ask shows "Run `swift test`?" on the iPhone, the Mac and the Watch within a second. That job waits, with its round clock paused, while the others keep going.
- [ ] "Yes, and don't ask again for `swift test` in oby" shows the rule before saving it, and the next `swift test` runs without asking. Deny beats allow (#67).
- [ ] "No: run only RunnerTests" reaches the agent as the denial message, and it changes course.
- [ ] Switching a running job from Ask to Bypass ("stop asking on the Watch job", or the job's Mode menu) answers its waiting prompt and the ones after it.
- [ ] Plan: the agent can't edit. Its plan arrives as a card with *Approve* (pick the mode), *Change it*, or your own words.
- [ ] In Bypass, `git push` is still refused.
- [ ] Codex jobs follow the same modes (`accept`, `acceptForSession`, `decline`).

## Build

- [x] **Engine:** `mode` on the job (`ask`, `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `bypass`), with the default in Settings. Policy's fixed denials run first in every mode, then the mode allows or asks.
- [x] **A waiting permission is a decision on the job,** like `question`: the tool, the command or file, and the suggested rule. It goes to the inbox and alerts the phone and the Watch. The answer goes back as Claude Code's `control_response` (with `updatedPermissions` for "don't ask again") or as Codex's decision.
- [x] **Plan:** Claude Code's plan permission mode. Codex runs read-only with a plan-only turn.
- [ ] **Rules** in `oby.sqlite` per repository, as #67 describes. They're listed in Settings, and saying "forget that" removes one.
- [x] **API:** `mode` on `POST /v1/jobs`, `POST /v1/jobs/{id}/mode`, `permission` on Job, and answers through `POST /v1/jobs/{id}/permission`, in docs/runner-api.md.
- [x] **Cards** on the iPhone, Mac and Watch use the same decision card as questions: the recommended option first, "type your own" last.
- [x] **Voice:** "allow it", "always allow that", "no, run only the runner tests".

## Will it work? Works

- Claude Code's stdio permission prompts and Codex's approval requests are proven (#37). Oby already answers every one of them; this feature hands some to you.

**Watch out**

- Oby never launches Claude Code with its own bypass flag. Oby keeps answering every prompt so the fixed rules still apply.
- On the Mac, agents don't run in bubblewrap, so Bypass relies on Oby's rules alone, as it does today.
- Waiting for an answer pauses only that job. Waiting time doesn't count toward the 45-minute round limit.

## Related

#7 (safe when nobody is watching), #65 (inbox), #67 (learned rules), #10 (Codex and Cursor), #118 (moving jobs, decision cards).

Claude Code has a `dontAsk` permission mode (`--permission-mode dontAsk`) that the launch dialog's Start-in segments never offer, and it doesn't appear when cycling modes in Claude Code either.

A session resumed from the Resume tab now comes back in whatever mode its transcript last recorded, `dontAsk` included (plan resume-and-dangerously-allow). Muster can therefore run a `dontAsk` session but never start one.

Explore what `dontAsk` does, measured against the pinned Claude Code version, and decide whether the launch dialog should offer it. `kb:adr/launch-bypass-and-dontask-unoffered` records why it was left out.

items.title: Run Claude Code inside a sandbox with automatic bypass mode
items.body:
## Goal

Run Claude Code itself inside an abox sandbox, and let abox switch it to bypass mode (no permission prompts) automatically, but only when the sandbox really contains it. Today Claude runs on the host and uses sandboxes through the MCP tools; this adds the other direction: the agent lives in the box.

"Automatic" means abox checks a fixed set of conditions. If all hold, Claude starts in bypass mode. If one fails, Claude starts in its normal mode with prompts, and abox says which condition failed. abox never silently weakens a sandbox to make bypass possible.

## Conditions for bypass mode

1. **Real isolation.** A container backend (Docker or Podman, later gVisor), not privileged, no Docker socket or other host control socket mounted, no added capabilities beyond the template defaults. Never on the `process` backend (`isolation: none`), because there Claude would run on the host.
2. **Workspace is a copy.** `copy`, `worktree` or `clone`; never `mount` with write access. With a writable mount the agent could change host-executed files such as `.git/hooks/*`, `.envrc` or editor task files without a prompt. Results come back as a diff with flagged paths (diff-apply, #48) for the human to review.
3. **Network is an allowlist.** `api.anthropic.com` plus the package registries the template needs (through the package caches, #14). Set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1` so telemetry and update checks need no extra destinations. `open` network disables bypass.
4. **Own, revocable credentials.** Never mount the host `~/.claude` or `~/.claude.json`: the policy forbids hidden folders, and they hold every host session and its history. Instead pass a dedicated long-lived token (from `claude setup-token`) as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, or an API key, as an abox secret. Document the residual risk: in bypass mode the agent can read this token. With the allowlist it can only send it to Anthropic, and the user can revoke it at any time.
5. **Started by a human.** Creating or starting such a sandbox starts an agent that spends the user's subscription. It is a human-only operation (`requireHuman` in the facade, CLI and GUI). The agent-facing MCP server must not be able to do it, otherwise an agent could start further agents that run without prompts.
6. **Runs as a non-root user.** Claude Code refuses `--dangerously-skip-permissions` as root ("cannot be used with root/sudo privileges"). There is an `IS_SANDBOX` escape hatch, but the container user should simply not be root.

## Claude Code settings inside the container

Found in the installed Claude Code binary; how they interact is **not verified yet**. Checking that is the first task.

- `permissions.defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` in the container's `~/.claude/settings.json`, as an alternative to the CLI flag.
- `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt: true`, so the bypass consent dialog does not block the first start.
- `hasCompletedOnboarding: true` in `~/.claude.json`, to skip onboarding.
- `IS_SANDBOX`: only if running as root cannot be avoided, which it should be.

The settings files are written by abox into the sandbox, not taken from the host.

## Proposed shape

- A built-in template `claude-code` (Node base with Claude Code installed, non-root user, allowlist network, `worktree` as the default workspace).
- `abox agent claude [<sandbox>] [-- <claude args>]`: creates the sandbox from the template, or uses an existing one. It checks the conditions above, writes the settings, injects the token and starts Claude in an interactive TTY (same path as `abox shell`). It prints one line saying whether bypass mode is on, and if not, why.
- `--no-bypass` to force normal mode. There is no flag to force bypass when a condition fails.
- GUI: a "Start Claude" button in the sandbox terminal tab showing the same status (bypass on, or the failed condition).
- Audit log entries for "agent started (bypass on/off, reason)".
- Docs: `docs/claude-code.md` gets a section "Claude inside a sandbox", and `docs/security.md` covers the token risk and the conditions.

## Tests

- Unit tests: the condition check returns the right reason for each failing condition (process backend, writable mount, open network, docker socket, root user).
- Facade: the MCP or agent context cannot create or start the Claude sandbox (`requireHuman`).
- Docker integration: the container starts as non-root, the settings files are present, and only the allowlisted destinations are reachable. Do not call the real API in CI: check `claude --version` and the written config. Verify a real login and session by hand and document that.

## Out of scope

- Other agents (Codex, Aider, ...). The same mechanism can be generalised later.
- Nested abox (abox MCP inside the sandbox).

items.title: Audit Claude Code permissions against the SDG needs list (draft)
items.body:
Agent: Product · Discovery · claude-sonnet-5-5

> **Status: DRAFT.** Depends on the runtime-neutral SDG needs list in #590 (W11) and the Architect's design. Candidates below are things to examine, not findings.

## Description
Audit the permissions a Claude Code session has when doing SDG work against the same least-privilege list used for Codex in #590: where today's access exceeds what SDG work needs, and what tightening is worth its cost. Claude Code's current setup is one data point, not a target. The maintainer applies any change to his own Claude Code configuration.

## Candidates to examine (not findings)
- Broad Bash with network access, against the needs list (read repo; write in repo and worktrees; SDG scripts; `gh`; no merge into `main` without confirmation).
- Allow rules narrowed to the SDG scripts and specific `gh` subcommands instead of broad ones (the same split as the Codex rules file: read-only versus writes, `gh pr merge` always prompted).
- Enabling Claude Code's optional OS-level Bash sandbox with the needed writable paths and network exceptions.
- Keeping the SDG hooks (branch naming, commit on `main`, merge guard, completion reminder) and the auto-mode classifier as a second layer, not the only one.
- Cost: more prompts and breakage; any tightening needs testing against real SDG runs before it is recommended.

## Boundary (draft)
In: compare today's effective access (settings, rules, sandbox, hooks) with the needs list; list excess and the cost of closing each; recommend per item (tighten, keep, document). Out: applying changes to the maintainer's config; the Codex profile (#590); merge autonomy (#511).

## Acceptance criteria (DRAFT)

### AC1: Excess is listed against the needs list
- Given the completed SDG needs list and the current Claude Code permission setup
- When the audit is done
- Then each place where access exceeds the list is named, with the evidence (setting or rule) and a keep, tighten or document recommendation

### AC2: Cost is tested, not guessed
- Given a recommended tightening
- When it is tried in a real SDG run
- Then the prompts and breakage it causes are recorded, and a recommendation that was not tested is marked as such

### AC3: Second layer stays
- Given any recommended tightening
- When it is adopted
- Then the SDG hooks and the auto-mode classifier remain active as an additional layer

### AC4: Hard limits hold
- Given the audit and its recommendations
- When they are read
- Then none recommends bypassing the sandbox or approvals, every merge into `main` stays behind the maintainer's confirmation, and nothing is applied to the maintainer's config by SDG itself

**Depends on:** #590 (W11, source of the needs list). Standalone item (TiesL decision 2026-10-27): not part of the #513 bundle
**Epic:** none (standalone by maintainer decision, 2026-10-27; listed in #513 only as a standalone neighbour)
**Blocked by:** #590 (the needs list and its Architect design, now on #513)
**Size:** S-M (first estimate; testing against real runs drives it)
**Runtime fit:** Claude Code

items.title: Handle bypassPermissions scope for Claude Code v2.1.257+
items.body:
## Context

Users who choose bypass during `repo-pattern setup` may believe the project is configured to bypass permission checks. Claude Code v2.1.257 and later ignore `permissions.defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` when it is set in project or local settings. Moving the setting to `~/.claude/settings.json` affects every project, so repo-pattern must explain that broader scope and obtain explicit confirmation before writing it.

## Current State

Verified on 2026-10-20:

- `scripts/lib/setup.mjs` reads `claude --version` for interactive setup and starts the setup wizard.
- `scripts/lib/setup-wizard.mjs` asks “Allow bypass permissions mode?” and notes that Claude Code v2.1.257+ ignores this setting from project config.
- `scripts/lib/provision.mjs` currently applies bypass to the project `.claude/settings.json`.
- `scripts/lib/doctor.mjs` collects checks and fails only when a check is false.
- `doctor` and migration are dispatched in `scripts/lib/setup.mjs`.
- `scripts/self-check/setup-wizard.mjs` asserts the current wizard note.

## Proposed Change

Handle bypass scope based on the detected Claude Code version and require confirmation before changing user-wide settings.

### Setup on Claude Code v2.1.257 or later

1. Explain that project-scoped `bypassPermissions` is ignored and that user-scoped configuration affects every project.
2. If the user selects bypass, ask for explicit confirmation before writing `permissions.defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` to `~/.claude/settings.json`.
3. If user settings already contain a different `permissions.defaultMode`, ask separately before replacing it. Preserve all unrelated JSON keys.
4. If `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` is set to `"disable"`, do not modify the file and explain that bypass is blocked by policy.
5. If user settings cannot be read or parsed, do not modify the file and report the concrete failure. Never report bypass as enabled when the write did not succeed.
6. In non-interactive `setup --yes`, do not enable bypass or modify user settings; leave bypass disabled and print a warning/instructions.

### Setup on Claude Code below v2.1.257

Keep the existing project-scope behavior unchanged.

### Doctor

Detect project `.claude/settings.json` with `permissions.defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` when Claude Code is v2.1.257 or later. Print a warning that this project-scoped setting has no effect. The warning must not fail `doctor`; doctor must not modify project or user settings.

### Migration

When migration finds the legacy project-scoped bypass setting on Claude Code v2.1.257 or later, ask whether to move it to user scope. If accepted, apply the same user-settings safeguards as setup, including a separate confirmation before replacing an existing `defaultMode`. If declined, preserve the project setting and report that it is ineffective. Do not copy, delete, or modify unrelated settings keys. Only `permissions.defaultMode` and `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` may be changed as part of this feature.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. For Claude Code v2.1.257+, setup explains that project-scope bypass is ineffective and user-scope bypass affects all projects.
2. Setup writes user-scope bypass only after explicit confirmation.
3. An existing user `permissions.defaultMode` is not replaced until the user separately confirms replacement.
4. When user settings disable bypass, cannot be read, or contain invalid JSON, the file remains unchanged and setup reports bypass was not enabled.
5. Non-interactive `setup --yes` never enables bypass in user settings and reports the bypass choice was not applied.
6. Claude Code versions below v2.1.257 retain current project-scope behavior.
7. Doctor warns about ineffective project-scope bypass on v2.1.257+ and exits successfully for this condition without modifying either settings file.
8. Migration asks before moving legacy project-scope bypass to user settings; accepting follows setup safeguards, while declining preserves the project setting and reports it ineffective.
9. The feature changes no settings keys other than `permissions.defaultMode` and `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode`.
10. Tests cover versions below, at, and above v2.1.257; unknown version; absent and conflicting user `defaultMode`; disabled bypass policy; malformed/unreadable user settings; interactive confirmation acceptance/refusal; non-interactive setup; doctor warning success; migration acceptance/refusal.
11. Every test states `protects=<observable>; fails_when=<wrong result rejected>; no_claim=<what green does not prove>`; code and behavior tests land together.

## Testing Plan

| Layer | What | Count |
|---|---|---:|
| Unit/self-check | Version comparison, settings merge, preservation of unrelated keys, invalid/blocked settings | At least 8 assertions |
| Integration/self-check | Interactive setup confirmation, `--yes`, doctor warning, migration accept/refuse | At least 6 assertions |
| E2E | Use CLI-level checks for prompts and resulting files if existing harness supports these flows; otherwise cover them through the integration self-check | Unknown until harness inspection |

Each test must carry its `protects / fails_when / no_claim` profile. Mocked CLI version output does not prove behavior against a live Claude Code installation.

## Rules for the Implementing Agent

1. Acceptance criteria define the observable each test protects, the regression it rejects, and what green does not prove; do not merely make tests pass.
2. Real code and tests land together; no placeholders or deferred tests.
3. Report any test, validator, CI, timeout, threshold, snapshot, or suppression change separately with justification.
4. Report only commands actually run and their observed results.
5. State what was verified, reused, and not checked; parent must independently re-execute reported checks.

## Rollback Plan

Revert the repository change. Do not automatically undo a user-approved update to `~/.claude/settings.json`; any user-scope rollback must be explicit and preserve unrelated settings.

## Effort Estimate

- Human team: approximately 4 hours.
- CC+gstack: approximately 15 minutes.

## Files Reference

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `scripts/lib/setup.mjs` | Version-aware setup/migration prompt and user-settings flow |
| `scripts/lib/setup-wizard.mjs` | Explain project-scope limitation in the wizard |
| `scripts/lib/provision.mjs` | Safely update user-scope permission setting while preserving unrelated keys |
| `scripts/lib/doctor.mjs` | Report ineffective legacy project-scope bypass without failing |
| `scripts/self-check/setup-wizard.mjs` | Cover wizard messaging and version-specific behavior |
| `scripts/self-check/mcp-and-settings.mjs` | Cover permission setting merge behavior |
| `scripts/self-check/doctor-output.mjs` | Cover doctor warning and success status |
| `scripts/self-check/provision-and-pipelines.mjs` | Cover migration acceptance/refusal and settings preservation |

## Out of Scope

- Modifying user settings from `doctor`.
- Changing settings keys other than `permissions.defaultMode` and `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode`.
- Changing project-scope bypass behavior for Claude Code versions below v2.1.257.

## Related

- None identified; the open-issue dedupe query returned no matches.

items.title: autopilot: model phases can bypass .claude/ protection via an interpreter
items.body:
## Problem

Claude Code protects `.claude/` (skills, agents, settings, hooks): in a `claude -p` run with `--permission-mode acceptEdits`, Write/Edit to `.claude/**` and recognised shell writes (`cp`, `>` redirects, `tee`) are denied. Verified on Claude Code 2.1.295 in a scratch repo: Edit of an existing `.claude/skills/old/SKILL.md`, Write of a new `.claude/skills/new/SKILL.md` and of `.claude/agents/a.md` are all denied.

But autopilot BUILD can still write there through an interpreter. In a `/deliver` run of a consumer repo, one issue's BUILD modified `.claude/skills/session-close/SKILL.md` with

```
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='.claude/skills/session-close/SKILL.md'
s=open(p).read()
...
open(p,'w').write(...)
EOF
```

and it was committed. The protected-path check only sees the tool's own target paths and recognisable shell redirects, not what a program does inside an interpreter. A sibling issue's BUILD (Write, `cp`) was denied three times and parked — so the behaviour is both a security gap and nondeterministic.

Consequences:
- A model phase can change the instructions, permissions or hooks that govern later phases (and human sessions) without approval. Not verified whether `.claude/settings.json` is writable this way; assume yes until shown otherwise.
- Whether a skill/agent change succeeds depends on which tool the model happens to pick.

## Proposed

1. **Detect, fail closed:** after every BUILD (and in `/deliver` final-verify before push), diff the head against the base for protected paths (`.claude/`, `.mcp.json`, `.claude.json`, `.git*` config). Any change there is a gate failure — a `protected_paths` gate in `loop.sh`.
2. **Staging convention (documented):** skills/agents go to a non-protected mirror (e.g. `staging/claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, `staging/claude/agents/<name>.md`) and are installed by a human-approved step after the run. The code-reviewer prompt should know the convention, so "not installed in `.claude/`" is not an in-scope finding when the charter says staging.
3. Optionally later, a narrow opt-in (PermissionRequest hook allowing only `.claude/skills/**` and `.claude/agents/**`), if Claude Code lets a hook override protected paths — unverified.

## Acceptance

- A BUILD that writes `.claude/**` by any route (tool, shell, interpreter) is caught by the gate; the issue does not merge with that change.
- A charter with the staging convention passes review without an "install into `.claude/`" finding.

items.title: Claude in Chrome extension permission popup fires repeatedly within an already-approved session, ignoring Claude Code permission mode
items.body:
**Description:**

While using Claude Code with the Claude in Chrome extension to fill out a series of web forms (data broker opt-out requests), the extension's own approval popup (a separate Claude-branded window, not a native Chrome dialog) re-triggered far more frequently than expected -- multiple times per page, including on actions within a page that had already been navigated to and interacted with successfully moments before.

**Steps observed:**
1. User set Claude Code permission mode to bypass/auto-accept.
2. Despite this, computer, navigate, find, and javascript_tool calls via mcp__Claude_in_Chrome__* repeatedly failed with: "No response to the Claude in Chrome permission prompt before it timed out".
3. The popup reportedly appeared as its own small Claude-branded window, separate from the main Chrome window.
4. Switching Claude Code overall permission mode had no effect on frequency.
5. Opening a brand-new tab sometimes (not always) temporarily resolved it, suggesting possible per-tab or per-domain state that is not being persisted/remembered correctly, or a race condition between tool-call dispatch and popup readiness.
6. Several calls also returned inconsistent results -- one type action landed in the wrong form field (text intended for one site form field appearing scrambled into a different field on a later site), coinciding with permission-timeout errors, suggesting actions may have been queued/retried in a way that caused cross-talk between intended targets.

**Expected behavior:** Either the popup should respect an explicit "always allow for this session" choice if selected, or Claude Code permission mode should be documented as not applying to Claude in Chrome (if that is intentional), so users are not surprised. The repeated popup-per-action within a single already-approved page is the core friction point.

**Impact:** Made a multi-step browser automation task (filling ~15 forms) effectively unworkable; user had to abandon the automated approach partway through.

items.body:
Environment for all five: AO desktop 0.13.5 on macOS (Darwin 27); `ao --version` prints `dev`, so the bundled build is identified by the app version. Two hosts (MacBook and Mac mini), each with its own daemon. Workers and reviewers: codex, claude-code (Claude Code 2.1.295) and others. Projects set `env.GH_CONFIG_DIR` to a dedicated GitHub bot identity. Searches ran 2026-10-09.

**Related:** [#817](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/817) and [#1754](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/1754) (same prompt, closed in May 2026; looks like a regression, or a new prompt variant), [#4888](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/4888) (workspace-trust dialog; closed), [#4895](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/4895) (open request for a launch-readiness hook, which would cover this), [#5751](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/5751) (`no_signal` rendering).

### Version info

AO desktop 0.13.5, macOS. Claude Code 2.1.295 (our notes say a Claude Code update introduced the confirmation; we have not bisected the exact version). Worker/orchestrator permission mode `bypass-permissions`. `claude -p` outside AO works.

### Minimal repro

1. Use Claude Code 2.1.295 on a host whose `~/.claude/settings.json` does not set `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt`.
2. Configure a project with a claude-code worker (or orchestrator) in `bypass-permissions` mode.
3. `ao spawn` a session.
4. Look at `ao session get <id>` after two minutes. Standalone, `script -q -t 0 /tmp/out zsh -c 'claude --permission-mode bypassPermissions -- hi'` shows the confirmation screen.

### Expected

The session reaches its first prompt, or AO shows that the agent is waiting on a startup confirmation (for example `waiting_input`) so a person can answer it.

### Actual

The `claude` process stays alive, no transcript is ever written under `~/.claude/projects/<worktree-slug>/`, the session sits at `no_signal` with no `reports` row, and the prompt never lands. AO does not answer the confirmation and does not mark the session as waiting for input. Every claude-code session on both hosts hung this way until we changed Claude Code settings (2026-10-09). Other harnesses were unaffected.

### Workaround

Set `"skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt": true` in `~/.claude/settings.json` on each host, then probe with one Claude spawn. After any Claude Code auto-update, probe one AO Claude spawn before starting a wave of work.

### Suggested ask

Detect the confirmation during TUI launch (screen text or the missing first hook signal) and either answer it when the project already set bypass-permissions, or move the session to a visible `waiting_input` state with the screen excerpt, instead of `no_signal`. Related: pass or pre-seed the skip flag in the same place the trust dialog is handled (#4888).

items.title: [Bug]: Claude CLI mode bypasses permissions and edits ~/.claude.json without asking; provider keys stored in plain text
items.body:
### Asyar Version

0.1.1-53

### Platform / OS

macOS

### Description

Found while setting up Asyar 0.1.1-53 (Homebrew cask) on macOS 26.7.1 with Claude Code 2.1.310. Code links are pinned to `334c8fa`. Thanks for Asyar, and for the Raycast importer.

## 1. Claude CLI mode always runs with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`

[`claude_cli_args`](https://github.com/Xoshbin/asyar/blob/334c8fa6717c7a09ac60e075395d20eba3e70f5b/asyar-launcher/src-tauri/src/ai/cli.rs#L726-L753) passes `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` on every run. The spawned `claude` loads the user's whole Claude Code setup: every MCP server in `~/.claude.json` and settings, plus Bash, Edit and Write. A launcher chat, or a silent agent fed from the selection or clipboard, can therefore run shell commands or call any MCP server's write tools with no confirmation. Text in a selection or a fetched page is enough to steer it (prompt injection). Asyar's per-agent tool selection and first-call permission prompts don't apply on this path. The `agy` path does the same with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` ([L825-L830](https://github.com/Xoshbin/asyar/blob/334c8fa6717c7a09ac60e075395d20eba3e70f5b/asyar-launcher/src-tauri/src/ai/cli.rs#L825-L830)).

Suggestion: run with `--permission-mode dontAsk`, limit `--tools` to what the agent selected (or `""`), and pass `--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <Asyar's server only>`. Asyar then stays the one deciding which tools an agent gets.

Workaround we use: set the CLI binary path to a wrapper that drops `--permission-mode` and adds `--permission-mode dontAsk --tools WebSearch,WebFetch --strict-mcp-config --setting-sources project`, run from an empty directory.

## 2. Asyar adds its MCP server to `~/.claude.json` without asking

[`check_cli_status`](https://github.com/Xoshbin/asyar/blob/334c8fa6717c7a09ac60e075395d20eba3e70f5b/asyar-launcher/src-tauri/src/ai/cli.rs#L189) and the Claude stream path ([L815](https://github.com/Xoshbin/asyar/blob/334c8fa6717c7a09ac60e075395d20eba3e70f5b/asyar-launcher/src-tauri/src/ai/cli.rs#L815)) call [`ensure_mcp_registered_for_claude`](https://github.com/Xoshbin/asyar/blob/334c8fa6717c7a09ac60e075395d20eba3e70f5b/asyar-launcher/src-tauri/src/ai/cli.rs#L711-L723). It writes `"asyar": {"command": "<asyar exe>", "args": ["mcp-server"]}` into the user-level `mcpServers`. The onboarding AI step probes every CLI on mount ([AiSetupStep.svelte#L71-L73](https://github.com/Xoshbin/asyar/blob/334c8fa6717c7a09ac60e075395d20eba3e70f5b/asyar-launcher/src/routes/onboarding/steps/AiSetupStep.svelte#L71-L73)). Settings → AI probes again whenever a provider is in CLI mode ([AiTab.svelte#L201-L205](https://github.com/Xoshbin/asyar/blob/334c8fa6717c7a09ac60e075395d20eba3e70f5b/asyar-launcher/src/routes/settings/tabs/AiTab.svelte#L201-L205)). So the entry appears before the user connects anything, and it returns after `claude mcp remove asyar`. The Codex and Antigravity paths write to `~/.codex/config.toml` and `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` the same way, when those CLIs are installed.

Effect: every Claude Code session on the machine (interactive, headless and scheduled) starts `asyar mcp-server`. That server exposes calculator, clipboard read/write, file read/write, **shell exec**, and web fetch/search ([mcp/server.rs#L46-L63](https://github.com/Xoshbin/asyar/blob/334c8fa6717c7a09ac60e075395d20eba3e70f5b/asyar-launcher/src-tauri/src/mcp/server.rs#L46-L63)). Users who guard shell access with hooks or permission rules on Claude Code's `Bash` tool won't catch `mcp__asyar__*` shell calls. Separately, [`register_mcp_server_in_config`](https://github.com/Xoshbin/asyar/blob/334c8fa6717c7a09ac60e075395d20eba3e70f5b/asyar-launcher/src-tauri/src/ai/cli.rs#L510) rewrites `~/.claude.json` by reading the file, editing it and writing it back, while Claude Code may be writing the same file.

Suggestion: register only when the user explicitly asks to, show what will be added, and offer a way to remove it. Or pass the server per run with `--mcp-config` and leave the user's global config alone.

Workaround we use: `"mcp__asyar"` in `permissions.deny` in `~/.claude/settings.json`.

## 3. Provider API keys are stored in plain text, but the README says Keychain

The README ([L379](https://github.com/Xoshbin/asyar/blob/334c8fa6717c7a09ac60e075395d20eba3e70f5b/README.md#L379)) says "API keys live in the OS keychain". The key field in Settings → AI ([AiTab.svelte#L738-L745](https://github.com/Xoshbin/asyar/blob/334c8fa6717c7a09ac60e075395d20eba3e70f5b/asyar-launcher/src/routes/settings/tabs/AiTab.svelte#L738-L745)) saves `providers.<id>.apiKey` through `updateProviderConfig` → `settingsService.updateSettings`. That method stores the whole settings snapshot in `settings.dat` ([settingsService.svelte.ts#L256-L257](https://github.com/Xoshbin/asyar/blob/334c8fa6717c7a09ac60e075395d20eba3e70f5b/asyar-launcher/src/services/settings/settingsService.svelte.ts#L256-L257)). On macOS that file is plain JSON at `~/Library/Application Support/org.asyar/settings.dat` (mode 0644).

Suggestion: keep provider keys in the Keychain as the README describes, or encrypt them with the existing keystore master key. At minimum, correct the README.

## 4. (minor) "Connect CLI" in onboarding replaces the provider's whole config

[`connectCliProvider`](https://github.com/Xoshbin/asyar/blob/334c8fa6717c7a09ac60e075395d20eba3e70f5b/asyar-launcher/src/routes/onboarding/steps/aiSetup.ts#L16-L26) writes a new object for `providers[spec.id]`, which drops existing fields such as `apiKey`. Merging into the existing config, as `updateProviderConfig` in the AI tab already does, would keep them. (Re-pointing the default agent at the newly connected provider looks intended.)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On macOS with Claude Code installed (`~/.local/bin/claude`), install Asyar 0.1.1-53 and go through the onboarding AI step.
2. `~/.claude.json` now has `mcpServers.asyar` (`<asyar exe> mcp-server`). Remove it with `claude mcp remove asyar -s user`; the next CLI probe (onboarding AI step, or Settings → AI with a provider in CLI mode) writes it back.
3. Start any chat in Claude CLI mode: the spawned `claude` gets `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` with the user's full MCP and tool setup (finding 1).
4. Saving an Anthropic key in Settings → AI writes it to `settings.dat` as plain JSON (code path in finding 3).

### Logs or Additional Context

```shell

```

items.title: Claude Code recognizer reads a prompt suggestion as a composer draft
items.body:
## Problem

After a turn ends, Claude Code can show a prompt suggestion: a guessed next prompt drawn in grey after the `❯` in the input box. On a crew's screen on 2026-10-22 the box held "Go with option C for seat growth", which nobody had typed.

The `claude-code` recognizer (`recognizers/claude-code.toml`, revision 1) reads the composer's value as the text after `❯`. Its first rule marks an empty composer only when the footer shows "? for shortcuts". Flotilla crews run with bypass permissions, and their footer shows "⏵⏵ bypass permissions on (shift+tab to cycle)" instead. So the second rule matches, and a suggestion becomes the composer's value, which reads as a draft. When flotilla adopts the composer guard (flotilla#3566), a draft blocks delivery, so a suggestion would hold up every turn to an idle Claude crew.

## To do

- Record a cast with a prompt suggestion showing, with and without a typed prefix, and add it to the fixtures. Note how Claude Code draws suggestion text (for example SGR dim) and where the cursor sits.
- Make the recognizer read a suggestion as an empty composer. If that needs selectors that can match cell styling, propose that engine change first.
- Record and cover the bypass-permissions footer that flotilla crews show.

Flotilla is also turning suggestions off for its crews (flotilla#3752, `promptSuggestionEnabled: false` and `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION=false`), but the recognizer must still handle sessions where they're on, such as a person's own sessions.

items.title: [Bug]: claude-code skill presents a throwaway git worktree as a safe place for --dangerously-skip-permissions
items.body:
## Bug Description

The bundled `claude-code` skill documents `--dangerously-skip-permissions` as an explicit opt-in, which is right. But it names a git worktree as one of the two places where that opt-in is acceptable. On `main` `69f73ec5f11f5a945cc864f29c4e2ad2307eaec3`, `skills/autonomous-ai-agents/claude-code/SKILL.md`:

- L121, *Opt-in: --dangerously-skip-permissions*: "Acceptable only in a throwaway worktree or isolated container."
- L286, flag table: "Throwaway worktree / isolated container only"

Anthropic's docs list three boundaries for this flag, and a worktree is not one of them:

- [Sandbox environments](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments): the documented choices for bypass mode are a container, VM, or whole-process sandbox runtime, with a non-root user. Restricting only the built-in Bash tool does not cover the session's file tools, MCP servers, and hooks.
- [Worktrees](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees): these separate edit locations, not all process access. The documented worktree checks do not follow every destination a shell command writes, and worktrees use shared Git metadata.
- [Dev containers](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer): container access still includes whatever is mounted or stored inside it; bypass mode does not prevent a malicious project from exporting that accessible data. Containers therefore do not justify an absolute isolation claim.

Following this wording can lead an agent to treat `claude -w <name>` as containment for a no-prompt session. The worktree itself adds no filesystem, network, or credential boundary; any such restriction must come from a separately configured permission or runtime boundary.

The sentence came in with #114781 (the fix for #113447, whose report suggested "throwaway worktree, isolated container"). That change's direction, bypass as an explicit opt-in, is right; only the worktree premise is wrong. This is separate from #136926 / #136937, which fix the timed `Enter` on the trust dialog and explicitly leave this section unchanged.

This is a documentation defect. It does not claim that a particular run escaped anything.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read `skills/autonomous-ai-agents/claude-code/SKILL.md` L119–121 and L286 on `main`.
2. Compare them with the three Anthropic pages above.
3. To check the proposed fix, save the diff under *Proposed Fix* as `bypass-worktree.patch` in a checkout of `69f73ec5` and run `git apply bypass-worktree.patch`. In a provisioned checkout, use the repository runner: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/test_skill_document_contracts.py -- -q -k claude`. The author checks reported below used the smaller fixture, not that full-checkout command: the new test passed with the diff and failed with only the `SKILL.md` hunks reverted.

## Expected Behavior

Bypass stays a documented opt-in. It is acceptable only when explicitly requested, with the whole Claude Code process inside a container, a VM or the sandbox runtime, run as a non-root user, and with known reach (files, network, credentials). A worktree, like the built-in Bash sandbox on its own, is not described as such a boundary.

Unchanged: the default permission-prompt flow, the `acceptEdits` paragraph (its "dedicated worktree" is about where edits land, which is a fair use of a worktree), and the warning-dialog steps.

## Actual Behavior

The skill tells the agent that a throwaway worktree is enough for a session with no permission prompts.

## Affected Component

Skills: bundled `claude-code` skill documentation (`SKILL.md` and its generated docs page).

## Debug Report

Not applicable. This is a documentation-only defect with no runtime involved.

## Operating System / Python / Hermes Version

Not runtime-specific. Inspected `main` `69f73ec5f11f5a945cc864f29c4e2ad2307eaec3`. All three relevant files were rechecked at main `3f2b1722b1e15b12e9ca199a19cb04012493288a` and match that snapshot. The test was run on Linux with Python 3.12.3 and pytest 9.1.1.

## Proposed Fix

Two sentences in `SKILL.md`, a focused contract test, and the skill page regenerated with `website/scripts/generate-skill-docs.py`.

What I ran (author checks): the new test fails on `main` and passes with the diff, and reverting either `SKILL.md` hunk alone makes it fail again. Rendering `main`'s `SKILL.md` with the generator's own `render_skill_page` reproduces `main`'s page byte for byte, and the page in the diff was rendered the same way. The test ran on a minimal copy (the exact test file plus `parse_frontmatter`, `-k claude`), not the full suite. The same diff also applies cleanly on top of #136937's head; the hunks don't overlap.

````diff
--- a/skills/autonomous-ai-agents/claude-code/SKILL.md
+++ b/skills/autonomous-ai-agents/claude-code/SKILL.md
@@ -118,7 +118,7 @@
 
 ### Opt-in: --dangerously-skip-permissions (isolated environments only)
 
-This disables permission prompts for the whole run — grants filesystem, shell, and network access with no prompts. Acceptable only in a throwaway worktree or isolated container.
+This disables permission prompts for the whole run — grants filesystem, shell, and network access with no prompts. Use it only when bypass was explicitly requested, and only with the whole Claude Code process inside an isolation boundary — a container, a VM, or the [sandbox runtime](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#sandbox-runtime) — run as a non-root user, where you know which files, network and credentials the session can reach. A git worktree (including `claude -w`) isolates file edits only; it is not a filesystem, network or credential sandbox. Neither is the built-in Bash sandbox (`/sandbox`) on its own: file tools, MCP servers and hooks still run on the host. Even in a container, whatever is mounted or stored there — including Claude Code's own login in `~/.claude` — stays reachable.
 ```
 ❯ 1. No, exit                    ← DEFAULT (safe choice)
   2. Yes, I accept
@@ -283,7 +283,7 @@
 ### Permission & Safety
 | Flag | Effect |
 |------|--------|
-| `--dangerously-skip-permissions` | Opt-in only: disables ALL permission prompts (file writes, bash, network). Throwaway worktree / isolated container only — see "Opt-in" above |
+| `--dangerously-skip-permissions` | Opt-in only: disables ALL permission prompts (file writes, bash, network). Container, VM or sandbox runtime only; a worktree is not a sandbox — see "Opt-in" above |
 | `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` | Enable bypass as an *option* without enabling it by default |
 | `--permission-mode <mode>` | `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions` |
 | `--allowedTools <tools...>` | Whitelist specific tools (comma or space-separated) |

+++ b/tests/skills/test_skill_document_contracts.py

+    _, body = _document("skills/autonomous-ai-agents/claude-code")
+    assert "it is not a filesystem, network or credential sandbox" in body
+    assert "sandbox runtime" in body
+    assert not re.search(r"throwaway worktree", body, re.IGNORECASE)
--- a/website/docs/user-guide/skills/bundled/autonomous-ai-agents/autonomous-ai-agents-claude-code.md
+++ b/website/docs/user-guide/skills/bundled/autonomous-ai-agents/autonomous-ai-agents-claude-code.md
@@ -136,7 +136,7 @@
 
 ### Opt-in: --dangerously-skip-permissions (isolated environments only)
 
-This disables permission prompts for the whole run — grants filesystem, shell, and network access with no prompts. Acceptable only in a throwaway worktree or isolated container.
+This disables permission prompts for the whole run — grants filesystem, shell, and network access with no prompts. Use it only when bypass was explicitly requested, and only with the whole Claude Code process inside an isolation boundary — a container, a VM, or the [sandbox runtime](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#sandbox-runtime) — run as a non-root user, where you know which files, network and credentials the session can reach. A git worktree (including `claude -w`) isolates file edits only; it is not a filesystem, network or credential sandbox. Neither is the built-in Bash sandbox (`/sandbox`) on its own: file tools, MCP servers and hooks still run on the host. +| `--dangerously-skip-permissions` | Opt-in only: disables ALL permission prompts (file writes, bash, network). Container, VM or sandbox runtime only; a worktree is not a sandbox — see "Opt-in" above |
````
